intervention_label: Rank-1 shared workup: germline BRCA1, PD-L1 CPS by 22C3, TMB on F1CDx, PIK3CA hotspot resolution, HER2 IHC 0 vs low, ITWG TIL re-score
expected_benefit: Locks the gating biomarker calls before the 1L systemic choice: germline BRCA1 unlocks olaparib/talazoparib on label (or routes to the somatic-BRCA Stanford trial NCT03990896 if the variant is somatic-only); 22C3 CPS gates pembrolizumab + chemo (KEYNOTE-355), SG + pembro (ASCENT-04), and TROPION-Breast05 enrollment; F1CDx TMB confirms downstream KEYNOTE-158 eligibility; HER2 0 vs low resolves T-DXd applicability; ITWG TIL re-score hardens the ICI rationale.
key_risks: None — non-invasive workup on archival FFPE + peripheral blood. Decision-tree risk if results return discordant (e.g. CPS discordance between breast primary and liver M1 in 20–30% of paired samples per pmid:34626408).
Turnaround timing: germline panel 2–3 weeks; 22C3 CPS 5–7 days; F1CDx TMB 2–4 weeks if a fresh order. Olaparib can start on a germline-positive result before CPS returns per NCCN v2.2026.
preference_alignment: Trial preference: satisfied (workup gates trial enrollment for TROPION-Breast05, NCT05534438, NCT03990896). Efficacy lean 0.7: satisfied (workup unlocks the cat-1 preferred regimens). Modality constraints: none triggered. Curative-intent framing: satisfied (germline status also informs risk-reducing surgery and cascade testing decisions for a 42-year-old with TNBC).
guideline_status: NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026 mandates germline BRCA1/2 testing for any patient diagnosed under 50 or with TNBC regardless of age. 22C3 pharmDx is the FDA companion diagnostic for KEYNOTE-355 / ASCENT-04. F1CDx is the FDA companion for KEYNOTE-158 TMB-H.
rationale_summary: Six gating tests in one workup. Germline BRCA1 is the decision-relevant dimension that the case is branched on — the rank-2 PARP-i row inherits scenario 'germline_brca:positive' from this result. The other tests do not branch the ranking (CPS gates a parallel set of regimens regardless of germline status, HER2-low and TIL re-score are informational), so they sit on this row as 'do these in parallel.' All five personas converged on the workup without dissent — no toxicity, no expense relative to the decisions it unlocks, and the only honest 1L conversation depends on the results. Concensusite is explicit that olaparib can start on germline confirmation before CPS resolves per NCCN v2.2026, so this is a workup row, not a workup-gate-the-whole-plan row.
open_questions: If germline BRCA1 returns negative (somatic-only), olaparib and talazoparib drop from the cat-1 label population; the somatic-BRCA Stanford talazoparib trial (NCT03990896) is the off-label substitute and the ranking shifts.
If 22C3 CPS returns <10, ranks 3 / 4 / 5 / 7 collapse; ranks 6 (SG monotherapy ASCENT-03), 8 (carbo/gem), and the CPS-low TROPION-Breast02 / TroFuse-011 lanes inherit the slot.
If HER2 IHC reflexes to 1+ or 2+/FISH-, trastuzumab deruxtecan (DESTINY-Breast04/06) becomes an off-label option for later lines; HER2 0 keeps it out of scope.

PIK3CA hotspot resolution is informational for this case — TNBC PI3K/AKT-axis trials (CAPItello-290, EPIK-B3) read negative or terminated, so the gate clarifies pathway biology rather than unlocking an active recommendation.
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic certainty. Gates olaparib (rank 2) on germline; gates ICI + chemo / TROP2-ADC + ICI rows on CPS ≥10; gates KEYNOTE-158 TMB-H on F1CDx.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — diagnostic test on tissue + blood)
overall: **The 1L conversation depends on six results; order them in parallel and start olaparib on a germline-positive return without waiting for CPS.**

expected_benefit: OlympiAD (n=302, BRCA1/2 germline HER2-neg mBC): PFS HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.43–0.80, p<0.001); median PFS 7.0 vs 4.2 mo; ORR 59.9% vs 28.8%. Replicated by EMBRACA (talazoparib, n=431, PFS HR 0.54). OlympiA adjuvant readout (pmid:34081848) shows iDFS HR 0.58 and OS HR 0.68 — the only PARP-i with a curative-setting OS hit, which strengthens the precedent for post-consolidation maintenance if the liver lesion is ablated.
key_risks: G3+ anemia 16.1% (vs 39% on talazoparib — the cleaner hematologic profile is why olaparib leads talazoparib on the same axis)
G3+ neutropenia 9.3%; nausea 58% all-grade; fatigue 28.8% all-grade
MDS/AML risk 1–2% on cumulative PARP-i exposure (per pooled OlympiAD/OlympiA datasets); baseline CBC and serial monitoring per FDA label
Treatment discontinuation due to AE 4.9% — the lowest among single-agent options on this ranking
preference_alignment: Trial preference: PARTIAL — olaparib is FDA-labeled, not a trial, but the alternative (TROPION-Breast05 control arm or rank 5 trial slot) keeps a parallel-track trial option available. Efficacy lean 0.7: satisfied (replicated phase 3 in this biomarker-defined population). Modality: oral, fits a 42-year-old with curative-intent framing and lower visit burden than chair-time regimens. Curative-intent framing: PARP-i can bridge to liver-directed local consolidation (rank 6) and extends into maintenance — the regimen layering is preference-aligned.
guideline_status: NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026: category 1 preferred 1L for HER2-negative mBC with germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant. ESMO MBC guidelines: MCBS v1.1 score 4 [I, A]. ASCO 2020/2024 systemic-therapy guidance concurs. FDA-approved on-label in this exact indication since January 2018.
rationale_summary: The strongest evidence package in the dossier for this patient: two independent registrational phase 3 trials (OlympiAD, EMBRACA) replicating PFS HR ~0.55 in the same biomarker-defined population, NCCN category 1 preferred 1L, and the lowest discontinuation-for-AE rate among single-agent options. Critic, concensusite, and conservative converge here on evidence quality plus guideline anchor. Risktaker dissented on the grounds that single-agent PARP-i 'collapses BRCA1 + TP53 + PTEN-loss + MYC-amp + TIL-3+ + TMB-14 down to one axis' and pushed for a chemo-free PARP-i + ICI combination (rank 10) instead — that dissent is preserved here and the multi-hit combination is ranked separately rather than displacing the cat-1 monotherapy. Olaparib leads talazoparib on hematologic tolerability (G3+ anemia 16% vs 39%), not on efficacy where the two are at parity.
open_questions: Germline-vs-somatic BRCA1 resolution is the rank-1 gate; somatic-only routes the patient to the Stanford talazoparib trial (NCT03990896, n=13 interim ORR ~38%) or to off-label use that the FDA breast indication does not cover.

Sequencing question: olaparib monotherapy as the 1L systemic backbone vs as post-induction maintenance after a platinum-containing regimen (DORA / MEDIOLA template). The dossier supports either sequence; the choice depends on whether the patient prioritizes oral single-agent versus chemo + maintenance.

Baseline ctDNA before olaparib start (target-validation row brca-reversion-ctdna-baseline) is the resistance-surveillance anchor — BRCA1 reversion is the dominant acquired-resistance mechanism (pmid:38302062) and the clean baseline lets the team distinguish reversion from off-pathway escape later.
likelihood_of_effect: High in germline BRCA1 HER2-neg mBC: PFS HR 0.58 (OlympiAD) replicated by HR 0.54 (EMBRACA, talazoparib).

counter_productive_moa.description: BRCA1 reversion / RAD51 fork-protection rescue is the dominant on-pathway escape (pmid:38302062); baseline ctDNA seeds reversion surveillance.

overall: **Two independent phase 3 anchors, lowest discontinuation rate on the ranking, oral single-agent — the cat-1 BRCA1 anchor that earns rank 2 in any synthesis that respects guideline fit and evidence replication.**
scenario_label: If germline BRCA1 pathogenic variant confirmed

intervention_label: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w + carboplatin AUC2 / gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² d1,8 q21d (KEYNOTE-355)
expected_benefit: KEYNOTE-355 (n=847, CPS ≥10 stratum): PFS HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.49–0.86, p=0.0012); median PFS 9.7 vs 5.6 mo. Final OS HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.55–0.95, p=0.0185), median OS 23.0 vs 16.1 mo — a 7-month median OS gain. The carboplatin/gemcitabine flavor pulls double duty against BRCA1-mutated disease (TNT pmid:29713086 BRCA-mut subgroup ORR 68% vs 33%).
key_risks: G3+ TRAE 68.1% (vs 66.9% placebo — the chemo backbone drives most of the burden, not pembrolizumab)
G3+ neutropenia ~41% on the carbo/gem backbone; G3+ immune-mediated AEs 5.3% (hypothyroidism, hepatitis, pneumonitis at single-digit rates)
Treatment-related deaths 0.4% (KEYNOTE-355 final)
ILD/pneumonitis class signal ~3% any-grade; baseline PFTs and active pulmonary surveillance per ASCO/SITC irAE algorithms
preference_alignment: Trial preference: PARTIAL — KN-355 is FDA-labeled and serves as the control arm of TROPION-Breast05 (rank 5), so enrolling on TROPION-Breast05 delivers this regimen under randomization. Efficacy lean 0.7: satisfied. Modality: IV chair time q3w + weekly chemo; user did not set a modality veto. Curative-intent framing: ICI + chemo is the deepest-response backbone available pre-consolidation.
guideline_status: NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026 (Feb 27 2026 update): category 1 — alternative slot after sacituzumab govitecan + pembrolizumab took the preferred slot on ASCENT-04. ESMO Living Guidelines: MCBS v1.1 score 4 [I, A]. FDA-approved on-label for PD-L1 CPS ≥10 1L mTNBC since 2020.
rationale_summary: Four-persona endorsement on the strongest CPS ≥10 phase 3 backbone — KEYNOTE-355 PFS HR 0.65 plus OS HR 0.73 is the defining 1L mTNBC survival evidence and the regimen's six-year post-approval irAE-management algorithm is mature. Concensusite reframed the rank order post-NCCN-v2.2026 elevation of SG + pembro (rank 7) to the preferred slot; this row is now the alternative category 1 backbone rather than the lead one. Risktaker dissented on preference fit, arguing the off-trial regimen wastes the TROPION-Breast05 control-arm slot — that critique is preserved and addressed by surfacing TROPION-Breast05 at rank 5 as the trial-preferred way to access the same regimen with a 50% shot at the experimental arm. The carbo/gem backbone is preferred over nab-paclitaxel in this BRCA1+ patient for the TNT-class platinum sensitivity signal.
open_questions: PD-L1 CPS by 22C3 is pending (rank-1 workup); CPS <10 closes this regimen and routes the patient to rank 6 (SG monotherapy ASCENT-03) or rank 8 (carbo/gem alone).
PD-L1 discordance between breast primary and liver M1 runs 20–30% in paired samples — order CPS on the breast primary block per 22C3 companion-diagnostic instructions.

If sacituzumab govitecan + pembrolizumab (rank 7) becomes accessible at the treating center, that regimen now sits above KN-355 in the NCCN v2.2026 sequence on PFS plus QoL; OS data are still immature for SG + pembro.
likelihood_of_effect: High in CPS ≥10 1L mTNBC: PFS HR 0.65 (mPFS 9.7 vs 5.6 mo) plus OS HR 0.73 (mOS 23.0 vs 16.1 mo) at final analysis.

counter_productive_moa.description: T-cell exhaustion / B2M-HLA antigen-presentation loss is the canonical primary-ICI-resistance route; rank-1 workup includes baseline B2M/HLA IHC for that surveillance.

overall: **The defining 1L mTNBC survival regimen at CPS ≥10 (OS HR 0.73, 7-mo median gain); now the alternative cat-1 backbone after SG + pembro took the preferred slot.**

intervention_label: Carboplatin AUC2 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² d1,8 q21d (PD-L1-agnostic BRCA1-directed backbone)
expected_benefit: TNT (n=376; BRCA1/2-mut subgroup n=43): ORR 68% (carbo) vs 33% (docetaxel); median PFS 6.8 vs 4.4 mo (HR 0.44); biomarker × treatment interaction p=0.01. CALGB 40603 (pmid:25092775) and BrighTNess (pmid:35093516) confirm carboplatin drives the pCR / EFS gain in neoadjuvant TNBC. Decades of carboplatin/gemcitabine 1L mTNBC experience back the class case.
key_risks: G3+ neutropenia 30–40%; G3+ thrombocytopenia ~15% (the dose-limiting cytopenias, manageable with G-CSF and dose holds per ASCO 2015)
Cumulative platinum nephrotoxicity rare with carboplatin; baseline creatinine clearance and serial monitoring
Predictable AE profile after three decades of post-marketing experience — no novel safety signals
preference_alignment: Trial preference: not satisfied (off-trial standard chemo). Efficacy lean 0.7: PARTIAL — TNT BRCA-mut subgroup ORR 68% is strong, but the n=43 subset has wide CIs and the regimen lacks a registrational 1L OS readout. Modality: IV q21d chair time; user did not set a modality veto. Curative-intent framing: layers cleanly with rank 6 SBRT consolidation after documented response — the most-experienced backbone for a converted-disease strategy.
guideline_status: NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026: category 2A among preferred 1L chemotherapy options for mTNBC; the TNT BRCA-mut readout is the indication-specific anchor for carboplatin preference over taxane in this patient. ESMO ABC concurs on platinum preference in BRCA-mut TNBC.
rationale_summary: The PD-L1-agnostic safe-haven for this patient: three personas (conservative, critic, concensusite) park it at rank 3–4 as the contingency if CPS returns <10 and PARP-i is declined or deferred. Critic is straight about the evidence: TNT BRCA-mut PFS HR 0.59 sits in a pre-specified n=43 subgroup with wide CIs — class evidence plus three decades of post-marketing safety, not a registrational 1L anchor. Concensusite layered a guideline-fit caveat in round 2 critiquing the critic's positioning: NCCN v2.2026 elevated SG monotherapy (rank 6) to category 1 preferred for CPS <10 / ICI-ineligible mTNBC on ASCENT-03, which now sits above carbo/gem in the CPS-low contingency stack. Carbo/gem stays in the ranking because it remains the most-experienced platinum backbone with the cleanest BRCA1 mechanistic fit and pairs with later SBRT consolidation more comfortably than SG monotherapy.
open_questions: After NCCN v2.2026 elevated SG monotherapy to cat-1 preferred for CPS <10, is carbo/gem still the right CPS-low backbone for this BRCA1+ patient? The platinum sensitivity argument is the differentiator — TNT class evidence vs ASCENT-03 generalist enrollment. Tumor-board call.

Carbo/gem as 1L systemic followed by olaparib maintenance is an off-trial regimen that parallels the DORA / MEDIOLA template (pmid:38236575, pmid:32771088). Not a labeled sequence; defensible mechanism.
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate to High in BRCA1-mut TNBC: TNT BRCA-mut subgroup ORR 68% vs 33% docetaxel (n=43, p=0.01).

counter_productive_moa.description: BRCA1 reversion under platinum pressure mirrors the PARP-i resistance route; serial ctDNA at progression resolves intra-pathway vs off-pathway escape.

overall: **The PD-L1-agnostic BRCA1-directed backbone; rests on a small TNT subgroup (n=43) plus three decades of carbo/gem experience; sits below SG monotherapy in the post-Feb-2026 NCCN CPS-low stack but pairs more cleanly with later consolidation.**

expected_benefit: Actively recruiting 1L phase 3 (n=1075 target) testing Dato-DXd ± durvalumab against the KEYNOTE-355 chemo + pembrolizumab backbone in CPS ≥10 mTNBC. Forward-cite anchor is TROPION-Breast02 (pmid:41937088): in CPS <10 / ICI-ineligible 1L mTNBC, Dato-DXd PFS HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.44–0.73, p<0.0001), median PFS 10.8 vs 5.6 mo. The TROPION-Breast05 readout is pending and the Breast02 effect size is cross-trial extrapolation, not a within-trial estimate.
key_risks: Dato-DXd: G3+ stomatitis ~6%; ILD/pneumonitis ~3% any-grade (characteristic deruxtecan-payload AE); ocular events; G3+ TRAE ~35%

Durvalumab adds pneumonitis ~3–5% any-grade — overlapping pulmonary-tox stack with Dato-DXd warrants baseline HRCT, PFTs, and a documented ILD-management algorithm before cycle 1 (conservative's round-2 caveat)

Randomization: 50% probability of drawing the KEYNOTE-355 chemo + pembrolizumab control arm rather than the experimental Dato-DXd ± durvalumab arm — the control arm is the same regimen the patient would receive at rank 3 off-trial
preference_alignment: Trial preference: fully satisfied (actively recruiting 1L registrational slot). Efficacy lean 0.7: satisfied if the Breast02 PFS HR 0.57 translates to the CPS ≥10 stratum, though the cross-trial extrapolation is the critic's load-bearing caveat. Modality: IV q3w, similar visit burden to KN-355. Curative-intent framing: layered ICI + TROP2-ADC mechanism delivers maximum systemic depth before liver-directed consolidation (rank 6).
guideline_status: Not guideline-listed — TROPION-Breast05 is an actively recruiting phase 3 with a pending primary readout. Concensusite flagged in round 2 that 'open phase 3 slot' is not the same as 'guideline-endorsed regimen' and the rationale for ranking it above KN-355 rests on preference fit, not guideline status.
rationale_summary: The trial-preference-anchored rank in this case: TROPION-Breast05 is the only 1L registrational slot that delivers an experimental TROP2-ADC + ICI arm without sacrificing the standard-of-care control (which is the KEYNOTE-355 regimen at rank 3). Advocate and risktaker both put it at rank 1 of their picks on expected-value grounds. The critic's round-2 caveat is the load-bearing tension: PFS HR 0.57 from TROPION-Breast02 (CPS <10 vs investigator's choice chemo) is being extrapolated forward to TROPION-Breast05 (CPS ≥10 vs pembro + chemo) — different population, different comparator, no primary readout yet. The honest framing is 'mechanistically aligned registrational slot' rather than 'PFS HR 0.57 forward bet.' Conservative qualified on toxicity (ILD stack); concensusite qualified on guideline fit. Rank 5 reflects the agreement-score gap (0.4 vs 0.6 above) — strong trial-preference fit, weaker board convergence than the cat-1 anchors at ranks 2–4.
open_questions: PD-L1 CPS by 22C3 is pending (rank-1 workup); CPS <10 closes TROPION-Breast05 and routes the patient to TROPION-Breast02 (NCT05374512, active not recruiting) or TroFuse-011 (NCT06841354, sacituzumab tirumotecan, recruiting) instead.
TROPION-Breast05 primary PFS readout is pending; no within-trial effect estimate yet.

Site logistics — TROPION-Breast05 sites are concentrated at academic centers; geographic accessibility may demote the row if the patient is not near an enrolling site (preference file does not capture geography).
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate (cross-trial extrapolation, not a within-trial estimate): TROPION-Breast02 PFS HR 0.57 in CPS <10 / ICI-ineligible 1L; Breast05 readout pending.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G3+ stomatitis 6%, ILD ~3%, ocular events; G3+ TRAE 35%)

counter_productive_moa.description: Overlapping pulmonary toxicity from Dato-DXd payload + durvalumab pneumonitis; baseline HRCT/PFTs mitigate but no combination safety dossier yet.

overall: **The trial-preference-anchored 1L slot — randomized against KN-355 with a 50% shot at TROP2-ADC + ICI; effect size still a forward bet on cross-trial extrapolation.**

intervention_label: SBRT to the solitary 1.5 cm hepatic lesion as consolidation on MSK SABR protocol (NCT05534438) after documented systemic response
expected_benefit: Curative-intent consolidation layer for de novo oligometastatic disease, layered on systemic response rather than substituting for it. SABR-COMET (pmid:30982687, n=99, mixed histologies): OS HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.30–1.10, p=0.090); median OS 41 vs 28 mo — encouraging but not statistically significant, with 4.5% treatment-related deaths in the SBRT arm. NRG-BR002 (pmid:33885704, breast-specific n=125): phase IIR PFS HR ~1.31 favored systemic-only, tempering the curative-intent framing. E2108 (pmid:34995128, n=256): no OS benefit from resecting an intact primary in de novo M1 (HR 1.11).
key_risks: SBRT G≥2 AE rate 29% (SABR-COMET); 4.5% treatment-related death rate in SABR-COMET — non-trivial signal for any oligometastatic ablation discussion
Layered on systemic therapy: requires 12-week response confirmation before SBRT and active multidisciplinary IR/radiation-oncology coordination
Honest acknowledgment: NRG-BR002 phase IIR PFS readout was negative; the biology-selection argument (de novo BRCA1+ TNBC, solitary 1.5 cm lesion) is post-hoc, not randomized
preference_alignment: Trial preference: satisfied (MSK SABR protocol NCT05534438 is actively recruiting). Efficacy lean 0.7: PARTIAL — biology-selected subset argument under negative parent-trial signals. Modality: hypofractionated radiation, manageable visit burden. Curative-intent framing: the explicit purpose of this row; the patient's preference free-text was written for exactly this conversation.
guideline_status: NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026 and ESMO ABC: do not endorse routine early surgical or radiation consolidation in de novo M1 disease outside a trial. NCT05534438 enrollment is the consensus-aligned route for a curative-intent SBRT layer (concensusite's framing).
rationale_summary: The genuinely split row. Advocate and risktaker both placed SBRT consolidation in their top 5, arguing that a solitary 1.5 cm liver lesion in a 42-year-old with BRCA1+ TNBC is the most consolidatable disease pattern she will ever present with and that the preference file was explicitly written to enable this conversation. Concensusite's rank 5 was a recommendation AGAINST routine early local therapy (E2108, NRG-BR002 phase IIR negative), with the caveat that NCT05534438 trial enrollment is the consensus-aligned route if consolidation is pursued — this is captured here as dissent on routine off-trial SBRT, not as a veto on trial-protocol enrollment. Advocate filed a round-2 dissent on concensusite's no-local-therapy position, arguing it overrides the patient's stated framing. The synthesis: status recommended on NCT05534438 trial enrollment after documented systemic response, with the cross-cutting caveat that the parent trials are negative and the rationale rests on biology selection. Critic and conservative did not surface SBRT in their picks (no dissent, no endorsement).
open_questions: What systemic response threshold gates SBRT enrollment? The MSK protocol gates on documented response on systemic therapy; the 12-week timepoint is standard but the protocol-specific definition matters.
If the team pursues SBRT off-trial rather than on NCT05534438, the curative-intent argument has no registered slot and rests entirely on biology selection against the NRG-BR002 negative signal.
Post-consolidation maintenance strategy: olaparib (OlympiA precedent, pmid:34081848) is the natural maintenance if the patient is on PARP-i at the time of SBRT; sequence-of-care varies by 1L choice.
likelihood_of_effect: Low to Moderate for OS in breast-specific oligometastatic disease (NRG-BR002 phase IIR PFS HR ~1.31 favors systemic-only); biology-selection argument for this patient is post-hoc.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (SBRT G≥2 AE 29%; 4.5% treatment-related deaths in SABR-COMET)

counter_productive_moa.description: Treatment-related deaths in SABR-COMET (4.5%) and negative NRG-BR002 phase IIR PFS are the load-bearing mechanism-level concerns against routine off-trial consolidation.

overall: **The curative-intent layer the preference file was written to enable; honest about NRG-BR002 negative, anchored on NCT05534438 trial enrollment after documented systemic response.**

intervention_label: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg d1,8 q21d + pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w (ASCENT-04 / KEYNOTE-D19)
expected_benefit: ASCENT-04 / KEYNOTE-D19 (n=443, CPS ≥10 1L mTNBC, BRCA-mut and -WT both eligible): PFS HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51–0.84, p<0.001); median PFS 11.2 vs 7.8 mo; median DoR 16.5 vs 9.2 mo. OS still immature at the primary PFS readout.
key_risks: G3+ neutropenia ~50% on the SG arm; primary G-CSF prophylaxis recommended per the SG label
G3+ diarrhea ~10% from the SN-38 payload (loperamide algorithm)
Pembrolizumab adds irAE pneumonitis ~3%, colitis ~2%, hypothyroidism ~15% — overlapping AE management on top of the SG cytotoxic floor

Treatment-related deaths reported in the cumulative SG dataset at 0.4%; the conservative round-2 caveat is that the rank position above KN-355 needs explicit G-CSF primary-prophylaxis and irAE-surveillance preconditions
preference_alignment: Trial preference: PARTIAL — ASCENT-04 itself is closed to enrollment; the regimen is now NCCN cat-1 preferred for CPS ≥10 1L. Efficacy lean 0.7: satisfied (PFS HR 0.65, mPFS gain ~3.4 mo). Modality: IV chair time SG d1,8 + pembro q3w — higher visit burden than KN-355 in the carbo/gem flavor. Curative-intent framing: deepest 1L systemic depth available pre-consolidation for CPS ≥10.
guideline_status: NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026 (Feb 27 2026 update): category 1 PREFERRED 1L for metastatic TNBC with PD-L1 CPS ≥10 by 22C3 — elevated above KEYNOTE-355 on the ASCENT-04 / KEYNOTE-D19 readout. ESMO has not yet published an MCBS score for this regimen; cross-society convergence is still consolidating.
rationale_summary: Concensusite ranked this at #2 — the only persona to surface SG + pembro in their top picks — and the NCCN v2.2026 elevation to category 1 preferred (above KEYNOTE-355) is the load-bearing guideline anchor. Critic qualified on evidence quality (the ASCENT-04 row sits at pmid:null in the dossier — conference data plus the NCCN elevation, with OS still immature). Conservative qualified on toxicity (G3+ neutropenia ~50% plus irAEs needs explicit G-CSF + irAE-surveillance preconditions). The board agreement score is only 0.2 because four of five personas did not put it in their top picks — but that reflects the freshness of the NCCN elevation and the conference-data-not-peer-reviewed status, not a clinical dissent. Status remains recommended because no persona dissented or vetoed.
open_questions: PD-L1 CPS by 22C3 is pending (rank-1 workup); CPS <10 routes the patient to rank 6 (SG monotherapy ASCENT-03) or rank 8 (carbo/gem).
Peer-reviewed primary publication is in press at the time of writing — confirm the citation when the manuscript locks.
OS interim readout will be the next decision-relevant pivot for whether SG + pembro stays above KN-355 in the consensus stack.
likelihood_of_effect: High in CPS ≥10 1L mTNBC: PFS HR 0.65 (mPFS 11.2 vs 7.8 mo); OS still immature.

counter_productive_moa.description: Same T-cell exhaustion / antigen-presentation loss concerns as KN-355; rank-1 B2M/HLA workup applies.

overall: **NCCN v2.2026 cat-1 preferred for CPS ≥10 over KN-355 on PFS HR 0.65 and DoR 16.5 mo; rank pulled down by single-persona endorsement reflecting fresh elevation and immature OS rather than clinical dissent.**

intervention_label: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg d1,8 q21d monotherapy (ASCENT-03 1L CPS-low / ICI-ineligible)
expected_benefit: ASCENT (2L+ pivotal, pmid:33882206 / pmid:38422473): PFS HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.32–0.52, p<0.001), median PFS 5.6 vs 1.7 mo; final OS HR 0.51, median OS 11.8 vs 6.9 mo. ASCENT-03 1L readout (CPS <10 / ICI-ineligible, including BRCA-mutated patients) was the basis for NCCN v2.2026 cat-1 preferred 1L elevation; effect size at 1L is the load-bearing claim — pending the full publication referenced by the NCCN update.
key_risks: G3+ neutropenia ~51% (primary G-CSF prophylaxis per label)
G3+ diarrhea ~10%; G3+ febrile neutropenia ~6%
Treatment-related death rate 0.4% in the cumulative SG dataset
UGT1A1*28 homozygotes carry higher febrile-neutropenia risk — genotype check recommended though not mandated
preference_alignment: Trial preference: not satisfied (off-trial FDA-approved single agent for the 1L CPS-low setting). Efficacy lean 0.7: satisfied. Modality: IV d1,8 q21d. Curative-intent framing: PARTIAL — single-agent SG monotherapy is less aggressive than SG + pembro at rank 7 but applies when CPS <10 closes that door.
guideline_status: NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026: category 1 PREFERRED 1L for CPS <10 / ICI-ineligible metastatic TNBC, including BRCA-mutated patients — elevated above platinum doublets in the CPS-low stack per the Feb 27 2026 update.
rationale_summary: Surfaced by concensusite in round 2 (critique 15) as the NCCN v2.2026 cat-1 preferred 1L for the CPS <10 contingency, displacing carbo/gem as the lead CPS-low backbone. The 2L+ ASCENT pivotal data are mature and unambiguous (final OS HR 0.51, mOS 11.8 vs 6.9 mo); the 1L extension comes from ASCENT-03, which informed the Feb 2026 NCCN elevation but is not yet a peer-reviewed publication in this dossier. Conservative kept SG 'in reserve for 2L' at their rank 4 — they did not surface the 1L extension, which is why agreement remains at 0.2 despite the guideline anchor. Rank 8 sits below rank 7 (SG + pembro) because SG monotherapy is the CPS-low version; both rest on the same NCCN cat-1 sequence.
open_questions: ASCENT-03 1L primary publication is the next decision-relevant pivot; the NCCN elevation rests on conference data plus the published 2L+ ASCENT backbone.
Sequencing question after SG progression: PARP-i, platinum-containing chemo, or Dato-DXd are the natural 2L+ choices; the dossier supports each on different evidence depth.
UGT1A1*28 genotype check before cycle 1 is recommended per ASCENT safety subgroup analyses; not mandated but useful for febrile-neutropenia risk stratification.
likelihood_of_effect: High in CPS <10 / ICI-ineligible 1L mTNBC (ASCENT-03 NCCN cat-1 elevation); replicated by ASCENT 2L+ OS HR 0.51.
toxicity_burden: High (G3+ neutropenia 51%, diarrhea 10%, febrile neutropenia 6%, treatment-related death 0.4%)

counter_productive_moa.description: TROP2-ADC mechanism — payload-driven cytotoxicity; no mechanism-level counter-productive vector specific to BRCA1+ TNBC.

overall: **NCCN v2.2026 cat-1 preferred 1L for CPS <10 / ICI-ineligible; the CPS-low fallback that displaces carbo/gem in the post-Feb-2026 consensus stack.**

expected_benefit: EMBRACA (n=431, germline BRCA1/2 HER2-neg mBC): PFS HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41–0.71, p<0.001); median PFS 8.6 vs 5.6 mo; ORR 62.6% vs 27.2%. OS HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.55–1.06, p=0.11) — not significantly improved at the primary OS analysis.
key_risks: G3+ anemia 39% (vs 16% on olaparib — the dominant hematologic burden)
G3+ neutropenia 21%; G3+ thrombocytopenia 15%

EMBRACA reported dose reductions in 53% and transfusion in ~38% of patients (vs 25% and ~17% on OlympiAD per the conservative's round-2 caveat) — materially compresses dose intensity over a 12–18 month treatment horizon
Same MDS/AML class signal as olaparib at 1–2% on cumulative PARP-i exposure
preference_alignment: Trial preference: not satisfied (FDA-labeled, not a trial). Efficacy lean 0.7: satisfied. Modality: oral daily, same as olaparib. Curative-intent framing: PARTIAL — interchangeable with olaparib on efficacy but the hematologic compression is the binding constraint.
guideline_status: NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026: category 1 preferred 1L for germline BRCA1/2 HER2-neg mBC (interchangeable with olaparib). ESMO MBC: MCBS v1.1 score 4 [I, A]. FDA-approved on-label since October 2018.
rationale_summary: Evidence-quality parity with olaparib at rank 2 — two independent registrational phase 3 trials replicating PFS HR ~0.55 — but the hematologic toxicity gap is meaningful. Critic ranked talazoparib at #3 and called the toxicity gap 'a tolerability not an evidence-quality concern,' which the conservative pushed back on in round 2: EMBRACA dose reductions 53% and transfusion 38% materially compress dose intensity over the 12–18 month treatment horizon for a 42-year-old on long-haul therapy. The synthesis: talazoparib is the contingency if olaparib intolerance emerges, not the parity choice. Rank 9 is below talazoparib's evidence-quality merit because the board converged on olaparib first; this row exists to make the contingency explicit rather than to compete with rank 2.
open_questions: Same germline-vs-somatic BRCA1 gate as olaparib; the somatic-BRCA Stanford trial (NCT03990896, n=13 interim ORR ~38%) is the off-label substitute for either drug if BRCA1 resolves to somatic-only.
Talazoparib hematologic toxicity may force dose reduction early; the EMBRACA dose-intensity compression argues against starting at full dose without baseline hematologic optimization.
likelihood_of_effect: High in germline BRCA1 HER2-neg mBC: PFS HR 0.54 (EMBRACA); evidence-quality parity with olaparib, tolerability is the binding differentiator.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G3+ anemia 39%, neutropenia 21%, thrombocytopenia 15%; dose reductions 53%)

counter_productive_moa.description: Same BRCA1 reversion route as olaparib; hematologic compression more often forces dose reduction than off-pathway escape.

overall: **Evidence-quality parity with olaparib (PFS HR 0.54) but G3+ anemia 39% vs 16% — the contingency if olaparib intolerance emerges, not the parity choice.**
scenario_label: If germline BRCA1 pathogenic variant confirmed

intervention_label: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID + durvalumab 1500 mg q4w as MEDIOLA-style maintenance after platinum + pembrolizumab induction
expected_benefit: MEDIOLA breast cohort (pmid:32771088, n=34): DCR 80% at 12 weeks; ORR 63%; median PFS 8.2 mo. TOPACIO/KEYNOTE-162 (pmid:31194225, n=55): ORR 21% all-comers, 47% in the BRCA-mut TNBC subset (n=15). DORA (pmid:38236575, n=45): 12-mo PFS 35.7% (combo) vs 11.8% (olaparib alone). KEYLYNK-009 (pmid:41405563): overall PFS HR 0.98 (negative); BRCA1/2-mut subgroup PFS HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.33–1.48, crosses 1, not powered).
key_risks: MEDIOLA G3+ AE rate 32%; G3+ anemia 12%, G3+ neutropenia 9%, G3+ pancreatitis 6%; 3 discontinuations for AE in n=34
DORA: nausea, fatigue, anemia dominant; G3-4 events scattered (<5% per term)
Off-label in 1L US TNBC — payer pushback is real and the regimen leans on single-arm + subset signals
BRCA1 reversion surveillance baseline ctDNA needed before olaparib start (target-validation row brca-reversion-ctdna-baseline)
preference_alignment: Trial preference: not satisfied (no actively recruiting registered slot for the MEDIOLA-style 1L US TNBC switch; concensusite's round-2 critique). Efficacy lean 0.7: PARTIAL — the canonical-responder phenotype rationale is real, the evidence base is single-arm + subset. Modality: oral PARP-i + IV q4w durvalumab, lower-burden than continued chemo. Curative-intent framing: chemo-free maintenance preserves depth-of-response after induction without cumulative chemo burden.
guideline_status: Not guideline-endorsed in 1L US TNBC. NCCN v2.2026 and ESMO ABC both list germline-BRCA-directed PARPi monotherapy (rank 2) as category 1 preferred for this patient; PARPi + ICI combination is not in the guideline-endorsed sequence outside trials.
rationale_summary: Risktaker's rank-2 pick on the canonical-responder hypothesis: BRCA1 + TMB-14 + TIL-3+ + APOBEC-flavored is exactly the phenotype where MEDIOLA delivered DCR 80% / ORR 63%, TOPACIO delivered 47% ORR in BRCA-mut TNBC, and KEYLYNK-009's BRCA-mut subgroup signaled PFS HR ~0.70. Critic dissented on evidence quality: a 'subset-of-subset stack of single-arm signals layered on a negative randomized parent trial' is not three independent replications; the KEYLYNK-009 BRCA-mut HR has a 95% CI that crosses 1 in a stratum that was not powered. Concensusite dissented on guideline fit: there is no actively recruiting registered slot for the MEDIOLA-style 1L US TNBC switch, and NCCN v2.2026 puts germline-BRCA-directed PARPi monotherapy at the cat-1 preferred slot. Two dissents on a non-veto option triggers `considered_with_caveats` per Hard Rule 3. The row stays because the canonical-responder phenotype argument is mechanistically clean and the post-induction maintenance template (DORA, MEDIOLA) is defensible in tumor-board discussion; it does not displace rank 2.
open_questions: Is there an actively recruiting registered slot in 1L US TNBC for the PARPi + ICI maintenance switch? Concensusite's reading is no; risktaker's framing is 'mechanistically clean defensible off-trial regimen.' Tumor-board call.

Sequencing: pembrolizumab + platinum induction (4–6 cycles) then switch to olaparib + durvalumab maintenance. The closest published template is KEYLYNK-009 (negative overall) and DORA (n=45 randomized phase 2).
Baseline ctDNA before olaparib (target-validation brca-reversion-ctdna-baseline) seeds reversion surveillance.
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate in BRCA1 + ICI-favorable phenotype (MEDIOLA ORR 63%, n=34); evidence is single-arm + subset, not RCT-grade.

counter_productive_moa.description: Critic dissented on the subset-of-subset evidence stack; concensusite dissented on guideline-fit (no registered 1L slot).

overall: **The chemo-free PARPi + ICI maintenance bet on the canonical-responder phenotype; held back by single-arm evidence stack and guideline-fit gap, retained for tumor-board discussion of post-induction maintenance.**

intervention_label: ZEN-3694 (BET inhibitor) + pembrolizumab + nab-paclitaxel on NCT05422794
expected_benefit: Phase 1b dose-finding (n~60) of ZEN-3694 + pembrolizumab + nab-paclitaxel in advanced TNBC with a pre-specified MYC-amplified expansion. No published efficacy data; the ZEN-3694 + talazoparib BRCA-WT TNBC phase 1b/2 (NCT03901469, n=51) returned ORR 22% — the closest precedent but with a different combination partner.
key_risks: **Conditional veto by conservative**: 'ZEN-3694 layered on pembrolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel stacks three independent myelosuppressive mechanisms with no dedicated combination safety dataset' — BET-i G3+ thrombocytopenia ~20–30%, nab-paclitaxel G3+ neutropenia ~30%, pembrolizumab irAE burden including pneumonitis ~3%. No characterized AE algorithm for the triplet.
BET-i class effects: thrombocytopenia, fatigue, nausea (per ZEN-3694 + talazoparib pmid not yet locked; ASCO 2022 abstract only)
NCI-sponsored trial at NCI sites only; geographic accessibility may demote on logistics
Phase 1b dose-finding — no characterized efficacy, no characterized triplet AE algorithm
preference_alignment: Trial preference: fully satisfied (active recruitment, MYC-amplified pre-specified expansion). Efficacy lean 0.7: PARTIAL — the MYC-amp + basal + TIL-rich axis is mechanistically aligned but no efficacy data yet. Modality: oral BET-i + IV pembro + IV nab-paclitaxel — high visit burden and additive AE stack.
guideline_status: Not guideline-listed. Phase 1b dose-finding; no NCCN or ESMO endorsement.
rationale_summary: The conservative veto is the load-bearing call here, contingent on the absence of a published combination safety dossier for the BET-i + pembro + nab-paclitaxel triplet. Three independent myelosuppressive mechanisms layered without a characterized triplet AE algorithm crosses the conservative bar — even in a preference file with no toxicity vetoes set. The veto lifts to qualified if dose-expansion safety with G-CSF primary prophylaxis and an irAE-management algorithm is later published (conservative's explicit condition). Advocate and risktaker both placed the row in their top 5 on MYC-amp / basal / TIL-rich axis alignment, but neither contested the veto in round 2. Per Hard Rule 1, a `veto_by` row from conservative or critic is never silently dropped — this row carries through as `not_recommended` so the reader sees what was considered and rejected, and the veto's lift condition is documented above.
open_questions: Has dose-expansion safety with G-CSF primary prophylaxis and an irAE-management algorithm been published since the conservative veto was filed? If yes, the veto lifts to qualified and the row may rise.
Geographic accessibility — NCI sites only; if the patient is not near an enrolling center this pick demotes on logistics regardless of the veto status.
MYC amplification confirmation (FISH or IHC, target-validation row myc-fish-orthogonal) is the trial-eligibility refinement; copy-number magnitude matters for the MYC-amp expansion.
likelihood_of_effect: Low for characterized efficacy (phase 1b dose-finding, no readout); class extrapolation from MYC-amp / BET-i mechanism only.
toxicity_burden: High (BET-i thrombocytopenia 20-30%, nab-paclitaxel neutropenia 30%, pembrolizumab irAE — uncharacterized triplet)

counter_productive_moa.description: Conservative veto on toxicity-as-mechanism grounds: three independent myelosuppressive mechanisms with no characterized triplet AE algorithm.

overall: **Conservative veto on cumulative toxicity without a triplet safety dossier; mechanism is aligned with the patient's MYC-amp / basal / TIL-rich axis but evidence is too thin to act on.**
